item.text: {"question_id":"7B.2","answer":"The 2023 record shows partial acceptance and attempted correction after the Constitutional Court invalidated the supplementary budget, but not completed remediation. Scholz acknowledged that the Court had the last word, said the government’s earlier legal assessment had been rejected, and described a supplementary budget, spending freeze, fund reduction, and proposed reauthorization of crisis assistance to comply with the ruling (BATCH-0016-E016; BATCH-0016-E017). However, the proposals’ final approval, implementation, and effects are not established. The response was also publicly characterized as non-specific and lacking an admission of error or remorse (BATCH-0024-E013; BATCH-0008-E017). Other adverse findings concern BAMF or coalition-government administration rather than a demonstrated personal Scholz decision: unlawful phone screening was judicially corrected, but a later law proposal reportedly disregarded that ruling; asylum counselling funding was delayed and insufficient; and disputed Russian-asylum information was said by NGOs to be outdated while BAMF reported later revisions (BATCH-0011-R01-E016; BATCH-0011-R03-E011; BATCH-0011-R04-E003). The data-retention response was Buschmann’s, not shown to be Scholz’s, and repeal was unverified (BATCH-0003-E008; BATCH-0005-E008). The Warburg material documents continuing memory-gap or denial claims and a reported correction of an earlier Senate denial, but no final finding that Scholz personally made the false denial or deliberately concealed facts; the supplied record also notes no proof of political influence and no initial suspicion of false testimony (BATCH-0024-E007; BATCH-0028-E010). Overall, the evidence supports partial institutional compliance and proposed remedy after a major ruling, qualified by incomplete implementation, public defensiveness, and limited proof of personal direction in the other
